newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on seasonal slide, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on seasonal slide, funds.

text.p: Fund selling, tied to long liquidation, and a seasonal slide pressured CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"The market can't go anywhere because harvest is right around the corner and we're already at historic high levels," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Traders said there were forecasts for drier weather in the U.S. Midwest next week which would boost crop prospects and speed harvest activity.
The market was underpinned by wet and cool weather in the U.S. Midwest late this week which slowed harvest.
The slow combining pace and only scant farmer selling contributing support to the cash basis market.

Technical selling ensued early when November soybeans rallied to a session high of $7.95-1/2 per bushel, just above first resistance near $7.94-1/4. Buying waned at that area which allowed local and scattered commission house selling to move prices lower.
First support in the November was at $7.86-3/4 and second support was at $7.79-1/4.
Soybeans closed 1/4 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with November down 7-1/2 at $7.83-1/4.

Refco Inc sold three million bushels of November, traders said. ADM Investor Services, E.D. and F. Man International, Rand Financial, Tenco Inc and Rosenthal Collins each sold one million bushels of November, sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 46,000, down from 62,903 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 1,000 $7.75 calls at 24 cents, Produce Grain bought 400 November $7.50 puts at 3-1/4 cents and Rosenthal Collins sold 400 November $8.25 calls at five to 5-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 19,000, down from 25,075 Thursday.
